MapBiomas is not field truth. Agreement is concordance with an annual map, often offset in time from the Sentinel-2 series.
Class 41 is a residual bucket. High overall accuracy against MapBiomas does not imply fine crop identity.

upcoming.name: Gaussian Process
upcoming.summary: Fits a smooth trajectory to a field's Sentinel-2 series and gives its 95 % interval, which widens where clouds leave gaps.
upcoming.status: Calibrated per region on fields in Bahia, Mato Grosso and Paraná, from another reading of the same Sentinel-2 scenes. It waits to be refitted and evaluated on series read by TERRA itself.

reads.label: Imagery
reads.value: Sentinel-2 L2A scenes over the polygon. A date counts when at least 30 % of the polygon is clear, and of two orbits on one date the clearer is kept

reads.label: Bands
reads.value: B02, B03, B04 and B08 at 10 m, with NDVI and EVI per pixel: the median over the polygon's clear pixels on each date

reads.label: Series
reads.value: The six medians projected on three principal components, each fitted with a Gaussian process of a seasonal oscillator and a local term, with heavy-tailed noise

limits: Calibrated on fields in Bahia, Mato Grosso and Paraná. Elsewhere it would use one scale fitted on the three regions together, which has not been checked outside them.
Coverage was checked on the three principal components, and in Bahia their interval is slightly wider than it needs to be. The NDVI interval built from them has not been checked yet.
The trajectory is smooth: a harvest or another abrupt change shows up spread over weeks, not as a step.

picture.subject: a soybean-then-maize field in Mato Grosso, September 2020 to August 2021, read as TERRA reads it: observed NDVI in orange dots, the model's trajectory as a green line and its 95 % interval shaded. Drawn with the model before its refit; the NDVI interval is not calibrated yet
picture.author: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2020–2021

upcoming.name: Observation noise
upcoming.summary: Gives each date of a field's Sentinel-2 series its own noise, from how many of the field's points were clear on that date.
upcoming.status: Measured on fields in Bahia, Mato Grosso and Paraná, from another reading of the same Sentinel-2 scenes: over 1 to 5 days, the noise's standard deviation is 2.6 to 5.9 times larger on dates with one to three clear points than on dates with all nine. It waits to be measured again on series read by TERRA itself, and to be packaged.
limits: The count of clear points predicts the size of the noise, not its heavy tail: the largest departures come on dates where every point was clear.
Dates with few clear points may also carry more haze and shadow on the rest of the scene, so not all of their extra noise need come from the count.
Measured on nine points per field. How it carries over to the clear pixels of a polygon, as TERRA reads them, has not been checked.

upcoming.name: Transient excursions
upcoming.summary: Marks the dates on which a field is briefly brighter in blue, or darker in blue and near infrared, than in the 15 days before and after, without the scene classification layer.
upcoming.status: Tested on fields in Bahia, Mato Grosso and Paraná, from another reading of the same Sentinel-2 scenes: it accounts for 26 % to 62 % of the excess in the noise's heavy tail in Paraná, and for less than 10 % in Mato Grosso and Bahia. Whether it becomes a model of its own or part of Observation noise is not decided.
limits: Weak in Mato Grosso and Bahia, where most of the heavy tail is something it does not mark.
After the marked dates are removed, the noise still has a heavy tail in every region.
A date is marked only when it departs from both sides in the same direction, so a change that lasts, such as a harvest, is not marked.

upcoming.name: Series events
upcoming.summary: Finds abrupt changes in a field's series, such as a harvest, and sets them apart from its smooth trajectory and its noise.
upcoming.status: A step detector over the Gaussian Process trajectory was tested and set aside: its false alarms stayed near 5 %, but it found only the largest injected steps. Detection from the trajectory's derivative is to be tested next.

upcoming.name: Radar noise by orbit
upcoming.summary: Gives the noise of a field's Sentinel-1 backscatter series for each orbit it is seen from: mixing orbits raises the noise's standard deviation from 1.37 dB to 1.94 dB.
upcoming.status: Its inclusion is decided, and the work has not started.
